Docusign Envelope ID: 68A6917E-AE67-83ED-83AB-E862A0396427




        October 12, 2026

        Re:      Transwestern Pipeline Company, LLC, Docket No. CP26-80-000

                                        COMMENTS OF STACK INFRASTRUCTURE, INC.

                STACK Infrastructure, Inc. (“STACK”) writes in support of Transwestern Pipeline Company's Green
        Chile Project, currently before the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or the “Commission”).
        This project will provide natural gas infrastructure to support Project Jupiter, the data center and microgrid
        campus that is under development in Doña Ana County, New Mexico.

                 As a proven developer and operator of digital infrastructure, including Project Jupiter, STACK
        recognizes that large-scale infrastructure development requires thoughtful planning around the supply,
        reliability, and the impacts on the surrounding community. On-site generation at Project Jupiter, through the
        Green Chile Project, will allow the campus to independently meet its power needs. That approach helps
        protect the reliability of service and the electric bills of families and businesses across southern New Mexico.

               Project Jupiter is already generating significant economic activity in New Mexico. As of September
        30, 2026, more than 1,200 New Mexico residents, including 630 from Doña Ana County, worked on the
        campus, and nearly $1 billion in contracts have been awarded to 30 New Mexico firms. These figures are
        expected to grow as construction progresses.

                Project Jupiter’s contributions extend beyond construction. Through partnerships with Doña Ana
        Community College and other programs, residents are gaining skills to fill the 1,500 long-term jobs that
        Project Jupiter is expected to create. The project has also committed $360 million in payments supporting
        local schools, infrastructure, and local services. In addition to covering the costs of water and wastewater
        infrastructure required for its operations, the project is investing an additional $50 million in local water
        infrastructure improvements that will benefit the broader community.

               Unlocking these benefits depends in large part on timely decisions. A project of this scale requires
        close coordination. Delays in the authorization of critical infrastructure will disrupt project schedules,
        increase costs, and create uncertainty for the contractors, suppliers, and workers involved.

                For these reasons, STACK respectfully requests that the Commission authorize the Green Chile
        Project as expeditiously as possible, consistent with its regulatory obligations. Prompt action will help
        ensure that Project Jupiter continues to deliver lasting benefits for Doña Ana County and the state of New
        Mexico.

                                                                       Sincerely,



                                                                       Mike Casey
                                                                       Chief Operating Officer
                                                                       STACK Infrastructure, Inc.
